Proof Lockup

Greet a cold reader with the two to four proofs behind a claim, each a figure they can check, between one short framing line and the promise it buys them.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1KickerOptional framing line above the panel, italic body size, never headline sizetext, fs-body
2PanelOne raised box holding every cell (not a card per proof); glass when the page defines it, surface otherwiseborder, ds-r-sm, glass, bevel, lift
3CellOne proof; cells split by hairline keylines, side by side from 40rem of the part's own width, stacked belowborder
4LabelMono uppercase, names the proofds-font-mono, fs-label, text-secondary
5FigureMono tabular figure, the one thing the eye lands on; side by side it scales with the part's width so it stays on one line (about 1.6rem in an 880px lane, never above the display step)ds-font-mono, fs-display, cyan
6CaptionWhere the figure comes from, in one linefs-body, text-secondary
7CloserOptional semibold line under the panel: what the reader getstext, fs-body

Usage

Use it when

  • The top of an overview needs the why-me in one look: two to four proofs, each a sourced figure.
  • The same facts would otherwise appear twice, once as a lede paragraph and once as stat tiles; this replaces both.

Do not use it when

  • Do not use it for a figure without a source on the page; a proof with nothing behind it is decoration.
  • Do not use it for five or more facts, or for a dashboard of live counts; that is the fact tiles or a table.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
kickerstringnoOne or two sentences. Body size, italic.
cells[]{label, fig, cap}yesTwo to four. fig is short: a count, a range, "n of m".
closerstringnoOne sentence.

Access

  • Cells are a real ul of li, so a screen reader announces how many proofs there are; each reads label, figure, caption in source order.
  • Meaning never rides on colour: the figure is cyan and also the largest mono text in its cell.
  • Layout is a container query on the part itself, so it is correct in any column; tracks use minmax(0, 1fr) and figures wrap anywhere rather than overflow.
